issue_context.title: TLS index that holds fipsctx->thread_event_handler is not freed
issue_context.body:
The FIPS-specific `thread_event_handler` is a pointer stored in TLS index https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2e966354956e55825331f61bf98976ffe60e4332/crypto/initthread.c#L269-L278

You may need to do similar to how `rcu_local_key` is handled
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2e966354956e55825331f61bf98976ffe60e4332/crypto/context.c#L348-L363

The problem is revealed by AppVerifier on Windows 10, with and without using a non-default OpenSSL library context.
comments:
I'm not sure I follow, The thread_event_handler is cleaned up in context_deinit_objs is called during context teardown.

What did AppVerifier show you?

> [...] The thread_event_handler is cleaned up in context_deinit_objs is called during context teardown.

This code in `context_deinit_objs`
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/81259299499e81d0b3850e09c9366aa67c65b07c/crypto/context.c#L320-L324
freed only the resource that `thread_event_handler` pointers to
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/81259299499e81d0b3850e09c9366aa67c65b07c/crypto/initthread.c#L297-L300
The TLS index created by `CRYPTO_THREAD_init_local` is still there.

> What did AppVerifier show you?

```
0:000> g
ModLoad: 00007ffb`b0cb0000 00007ffb`b1354000   [some].dll
ModLoad: 00007ffc`85b30000 00007ffc`85c8e000   C:\windows\System32\CRYPT32.dll
ModLoad: 00007ffb`bc630000 00007ffb`bc992000   [path]\fips.dll


=======================================
VERIFIER STOP 0000000000000350: pid 0xB69C: Unloading DLL that allocated TLS index that was not freed. 

	000000000019ABBA : TLS index
	00007FFBBC7B133D : Address of the code that allocated this TLS index.
	000001AB39442FE6 : DLL name address. Use du to dump it.
	00007FFBBC630000 : DLL base address.


=======================================
This verifier stop is continuable.
After debugging it use `go' to continue.

=======================================
```

The individual thread context objects should be deallocated when the threads that allocated them exit, or when the library context that allocated that correspond to them are freed.

The fact that this occurs when (ostensibly the libcrypto and fips dlls are unloaded suggests that you have a thread which is still running with openssl library context at the time of cleanup.

Do you have a minimal reproducer that illustrates this behavior?

> The fact that this occurs when (ostensibly the libcrypto and fips dlls are unloaded suggests that you have a thread which is still running with openssl library context at the time of cleanup.

I have only the main thread.

> 
> Do you have a minimal reproducer that illustrates this behavior?

I have a minimal reproduce, but it's still the company's code, and I don't think I can share it. But it's very simple: `some.dll` is a library that links a static copy of `libcrypto` that has `no_pinshared`. An `.exe` `LoadLibrary` `some.dll`, calling into a function in `some.dll`, and unloads it. The function in `some.dll` does the following:
```
OSSL_LIB_CTX_new
OSSL_PROVIDER_set_default_search_path
OSSL_LIB_CTX_load_config
OSSL_PROVIDER_load(fips)
OSSL_PROVIDER_load(base)
X509_new_ex
d2i_X509
X509_free
OSSL_PROVIDER_unload(base)
OSSL_PROVIDER_unload(fips)
OSSL_LIB_CTX_free
```

You can email me to schedule a Zoom call to see it.

I believe that the ordering of the last two calls is the problem.  I'm not 100% sure, and its a bit counter-intuitive, but freeing the libctx that you've allocated call OPENSSL_thread_stop, which triggers all the needed callbacks to cleanup the allocations made in your main thread against the thread_event_handler key, prior to the OSSL_PROVIDER_unload call unloading the DLL.

Try backing out your proposed changed, and reversing those last two calls, and I think the problem will abate.

I'm not 100% sure, and its a bit counter-intuitive, but freeing the libctx that you've allocated call OPENSSL_thread_stop, which triggers all the needed callbacks to cleanup the allocations made in your main thread against the thread_event_handler key, prior to the OSSL_PROVIDER_unload call unloading the DLL.

review_comments: The style checker is catching this.  I know this didn't introduce it, but coding style says that, if you have a conditional with only one statement, you don't put curly braces around it.  Removing the curly braces here will get the style check ci job to pass
